summary: This article explains how gymnastics blends strength, flexibility, and balance, the apparatus athletes train on, and how coaches help gymnasts build precision and control.
introduce: Show the title “Gymnastics: Strength and Balance” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a piece of equipment used for a sport or exercise
a set series of moves performed in order
able to bend or stretch easily

challengeTerms.def: a particular way of performing a skill or movement
the force a moving body builds up and carries forward
controlled, steady effort to follow rules and train regularly

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that gymnastics takes more strength than most other sports? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why gymnasts need both strength and flexibility.
struggling: Pre-teach apparatus, routine, and flexible with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses technique, momentum, and discipline to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
